lines.t: Welcome to Concord landing. Every Tuner who reaches the Spire sits by this fire first. Most of them shake a little.
Rest your troupe? Open the Fosterage ledger? Or just catching your breath?

options.label: Help a kin recall a move

lines.t: Kiosk's open! Everything in Cantarra, at Spire prices. The view is included. The view is the expensive part.
The door remembers your chord now. Walk on — the landing's yours, and so is whatever waits on it.
Six sockets, shaped like tuning forks. Your Keynotes hum as you approach.
Go on — seat them. One for each hall you out-sang.
Root, stone, water, gale, fire, frost. Six notes ring out — and the stone door folds open like a hand.
Six sockets, and you're carrying fewer than six Keynotes. The door is very polite about it, but it won't budge.
That was the best I've ever played. And you were better. Go on — she's waiting.
Took you long enough! I've been standing here being dramatic in the wind for ages.
No jokes this time. Just — play your best, okay? I want to lose to the *real* you. Or win. Winning's also fine.
Door's still shut on your side! Seat your Keynotes, {player}. I'm not battling through a wall. I tried. It hurt.
There it is. That's a sound I've not heard in a long time. Sound the Great Chord, {player}.
And go and see Oriel. She came up the lift the moment the stones started singing. She hasn't stopped grinning.
So. You're the one who beat my kid on the landing. They're smiling about it, which is new.
I've watched my kid chase my shadow for two years. You're the first one who made them turn around.
Now — show me what *you* sound like.
Not yet, {player}. Somebody in a very long scarf is waiting for you on the landing. Don't keep them.
{player}. Look at you. Look at all of you. I came up the lift in my apron — I didn't even stop to take it off.
She cried in the lift. Twice. The liftkeeper offered her a hanky and she used his sleeve.
Hush. Now then — the Great Chord. Six Keynotes, your troupe, and every stone listening. Go on.
Six Keynotes ring. Your {starter} sings, your troupe joins in — and far below, every Chordstone in Cantarra answers.
…Okay. That was the best sound I've ever heard. Don't tell Mum I said it wasn't her.
Odile left me a letter. We'll read it together at the workshop. I think she wants to help keep watch on the stones.
At dawn, the Larkhollow Chordstone hums. Oriel stands beside it with her eyes closed, listening.
There it is. Same song. New verse.
Everything hums again. Even my kettle, which is frankly unnecessary.
Word is the Old Chord Shrine on Thistledown Way woke up too. It wants a Gleam, I'd wager. Go and have a look.
Two losses at the top of the world. I'm framing both. Rematch again in a month? I'll bring snacks this time.
So. Champion of Cantarra. Mum's thrilled. I'm thrilled! I'm also… a tiny bit itchy to battle you again.
No titles, no Spire, no pressure. Just my team at full strength. Level fifty-five. Every one of them mine.
Mum says you play like someone who listens first. I'm going to try that. Quietly. For about a minute.
Six sockets, shaped like tuning forks. Your Keynotes hum as you approach.
No jokes this time. Just — play your best, okay? I want to lose to the *real* you. Or win. Winning's also fine.
That was the best I've ever played. And you were better. Go on — she's waiting.
I… beat you? At the Spire? Okay. Heal up. Try again. I want you to see her.
I've watched my kid chase my shadow for two years. You're the first one who made them turn around. Now — show me what *you* sound like.
There it is. That's a sound I've not heard in a long time. Sound the Great Chord, {player}.
Close. Very close. Rest, and come back — the Spire isn't going anywhere.
There it is. Same song. New verse.
